idiom_name: thin http.Handler/main + plain service functions over small interfaces (go test, net/http/httptest)
implementation_notes: Go's local idiom replaces the humble class: keep main and the http.Handler thin - decode the request, call a plain function or method, encode the result - and put the decisions in ordinary funcs and structs that go test drives directly. Collaborators are declared as the small interfaces the consumer actually needs (the io.Writer style Effective Go describes), so a test passes a fake without a mocking framework, and net/http/httptest exercises whatever handler glue remains when it needs checking. The classic adapter is worth keeping when a legacy framework type must be adapted, but the decision itself is normally a plain function call, not a class hierarchy.
pitfalls: Decisions creep into the handler: defaulting, rounding and validation written between decode and call stay untested while the service tests remain green; the handler should contain no branch beyond error mapping.

Testing a handler against a concrete service forces real dependencies; accept an interface (or a function field) so the shell can be given a fake, and use net/http/httptest for request and response wiring.
Table-driven tests whose rows need different arrange code turn into a switch inside the loop; split those cases into separate Test functions instead of hiding the setup.
